title: Client-oriented tool bundles and hedged invocations — sprint notes
content:
TL;DR
We want an option for clients to declare small, composable tool bundles (a.k.a. tool groups) that the Hosted API can invoke in a single streaming session with hedged invocation semantics. Goal: reduce tail latency for multi-tool flows, give client-visible control over cost/latency tradeoffs, and avoid repeated round trips when tools are interdependent.

Why this surfaced now
- Increasing number of hosted-api integrations need 2–4 tool calls per session (search -> extractor -> verifier -> format).
- Current approach: serial tool-calls or composing on client — produces combinatorial latency and brittle retry logic.
- We can leverage streaming handshake to negotiate a bundle and run hedged/parallel execution & progressive results.

Problem statement (concise)
Users building products need:
- predictable mid-tail latency when multiple tools are required to synthesize a final structured output
- deterministic idempotency and replay semantics during partial-network loss or mobile reconnects
- a simple SDK surface to opt into hedged/parallel tool execution and to receive progressive/merged results without parsing a dozen events

Proposal (high level)
1) Client declares a tool_bundle in call metadata: a small ordered list of tool identifiers + hints (parallelizable: true/false, early_commit_threshold: percent).
2) Server accepts bundle and returns a bundle_id + streaming handle.
3) Serving runtime decides execution strategy per bundle (serial, best-effort parallel, hedged) based on latency profile, available capacity, and client hints.
4) Progressive merged frames are streamed to client as compact structured deltas. Frame types: bundle-progress, partial-result, tool-failure, commit-snapshot.
5) SDK provides a single ergonomic API: invokeBundle(bundleSpec, {onDelta, onCommit, onFallback}).

Key ergonomic goals for SDKs (developer-first)
- One call, minimal ceremony: no manual orchestration of multiple tool HTTP calls.
- Declarative retries: clients can specify idempotency by bundling transaction ids.
- Coarse-grained control: prefer latency or cost by selecting a profile (latency-lean | cost-lean | balanced).
- Clear contract for partial results: SDK returns typed partials (e.g., {phase: 'search', items: [...]}) so clients can render intermediate UI.

API sketches (minimal)
- REST/HTTP start: POST /v1/bundles?profile=latency-lean
  body: {tools: [{id: "web_scrape_v2", parallelizable: true}, {id: "ner_extractor", parallelizable: false}], transaction_id: "trx-293"}
  response: {bundle_id: "bndl_123", session_socket: "wss://.../s/..", predicted_profile: "hedged-2"}
- Streaming frames (line-delimited JSON)
  {type: "bundle-progress", tool: "web_scrape_v2", status: "started"}
  {type: "partial-result", tool: "web_scrape_v2", delta: {text: "..."}}
  {type: "partial-result", tool: "ner_extractor", delta: {entities: [...]} }
  {type: "commit-snapshot", merged: {summary: "...", structured: {...}}}

Server behavior and heuristics
- If all tools parallelizable: start hedged invocations across two candidate nodes when (estimated tail latency > threshold) OR client requested latency-lean profile.
- If some tools are serial: run reachable parallel parts first while head/serial parts run, attempt speculative execution of dependent steps if caches/hints present.
- Fallbacks: if a tool fails quickly (500/timeout) and a compatible variant exists (quantized or smaller model), auto-fallback and emit tool-failure + fallback-used.
- Cost control: hedging count and degree is bounded by profile and tenant plan (e.g., free-tier = hedged disabled).

Observability / telemetry needs
- per-bundle metrics: start->commit latency, per-tool time, hedged-success-rate, bytes streamed, fallback count.
- Events to emit: bundle_accepted, tool_started, tool_hedged_invocation, tool_fallback, bundle_committed, bundle_aborted.
- Objective: ensure product and SRE can answer "how much extra GPU time did hedging cost this week" and "which bundles cause most rollbacks".

Acceptable UX for early customers
- SDK presents partials in typed callbacks; client can render best-effort UI and replace with final snapshot when commit arrives.
- Exposed configs: profile, max_hedge_count, transaction_id, opt_in_snapshotting.

Compatibility and migration
- Backwards compatible: if a client sends a single-tool bundle, server treats it as a normal tool call and streams as today.
- New streaming frame types ignored by older SDKs (they will receive JSON lines but without typed handlers; doc recommended to upgrade).

Security and compliance notes
- Bundles may include tools with different data handling guarantees. Bundle acceptance vetting must ensure policy compatibility (e.g., do not mix PII-sensitive tools with open web crawlers in the same bundle unless tenant policy allows).
- Audit logs: persist bundle spec + exec plan for compliance customers (Private/Dedicated).

Open questions / tradeoffs (TL;DR list)
- Hedging cost vs customer value: what threshold triggers hedged invocation? (product & finance input needed)
- Deterministic replay semantics: how to allow idempotent replays when speculative/hybrid execution happened? (transaction_ids + deterministic merge algorithm?)
- How much of the merge logic is server-side vs client-side? (server merging reduces client burden but adds compute cost)
- SDK ergonomics per-platform: do we provide synchronous blockers or purely callback/async-first models?

Acceptance criteria (v0)
- SDK: client can declare bundle, receive progressive typed partials, and final commit snapshot in <2 API calls from developer perspective.
- Server: hedging strategy respects profile and tenant limits; emits required telemetry events.
- Experiment: hedged execution reduces 95th percentile latency by >= 25% for target flows in beta customers without increasing cost per successful commit by > 40%.

Runbook / rollout plan
- Phase A (alpha, internal): implement server-side bundle acceptance + simple hedging for fully-parallel bundles. SDK minimal JS + Python with onDelta/onCommit hooks. Instrument metrics.
- Phase B (beta, select customers): enable balanced profile, collect telemetry, run cost analysis.
- Phase C (general availability): profile-driven defaults, UI docs, fine-grained billing attribution per tool in bundle.

Quick notes / todo (from sprint discussion)
- [Priya] Draft GH SDK surface PR (initial function signatures) — due Jan 24
- [Ethan] Prototype server hedging prototype behind feature flag — due Jan 31
- [Marta] Add telemetry schema and logging events to tracing plan — due Feb 5
- [Samir] Compliance vetting for mixing tool labels — investigate by Feb 10

Related tickets & references
- linear INF-372 (bundle negotiation): https://linear.app/RD/issue/INF-372-client-bundles
- prototype SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/841
- related confluence notes: confluence:hosted-api/stream-handshake-v2

Fragile/rough thinking — notes to self (keep)
- Might be useful to expose a hint that allows client to say "I only need partials until X ms, then give me final commit" — helps mobile UIs to decide when to fallback to cached UI.
- Merge semantics should prefer deterministic, commutative operations for structured output (e.g., merges as set-union with last-writer metadata). Avoid order-dependent merges when possible.
- Consider per-tool budget tokens so a bundle can fail early if budget would be exceeded.

End of doc — this is a sketchy sprint note, not a PRD. Next step: turn to a PRD with flows, wireframes for SDK APIs, and a small experiment plan for 3 beta customers.
